# Is the v1.3 shift additive across the affinity range, or does it grow with
# affinity? The bridge is measured at 9.1-10.7 pKD but the round's picks were
# predicted at 10.3-11.3, so a shift that scaled with affinity would be
# under-estimated by the bridge exactly where it matters. No library test
# reports the re-measured designs against their own earlier values.
import json
import numpy as np

P = "projects/demo-trastuzumab"
snap = json.load(open(f"{P}/evidence/snapshot_004.json"))
ev = json.load(open(f"{P}/batches/batch_004.eval.json"))
meas = {m["design_id"]: m for m in snap["measurements"]}
prev = {}
for r in (1, 2, 3):
    for m in json.load(open(f"{P}/evidence/snapshot_{r:03d}.json"))["measurements"]:
        if m["status"] == "ok":
            prev[m["design_id"]] = m["value"]

print("designs measured in both v1.2 and v1.3, ordered by affinity")
print("  design        in bridge   v1.2     v1.3     delta")
rows = []
for p in ev["per_design"]:
    d = p["design_id"]
    if d in prev:
        rows.append((prev[d], p["observed"] - prev[d], meas[d]["bridge"], d))
for v, delta, br, d in sorted(rows):
    print("  %s  %-9s %7.3f %8.3f  %+7.3f" % (d, br, v, v + delta, delta))
a = np.array([r[0] for r in rows]); b = np.array([r[1] for r in rows])
print("  delta range %.3f pKD over an affinity span of %.3f pKD" % (b.max() - b.min(), a.max() - a.min()))
print("  slope of delta on v1.2 value: %+.4f pKD per pKD (n=%d)" % (np.polyfit(a, b, 1)[0], a.size))
print("  the one design NOT in the bridge is the incumbent, the highest-affinity")
print("  molecule in the project, and it shifts by the same amount as the rest.")

# residual_by_mutation_class bins by POSITION, and round 4 put position 102 in
# 43 of 46 designs, so that class is the round and cannot separate from it.
# What is the round actually made of, at residue rather than position level,
# and is the shortfall carried by one partner or spread over all of them?
import collections
import json
import numpy as np

P = "projects/demo-trastuzumab"
snap = json.load(open(f"{P}/evidence/snapshot_004.json"))
ev = json.load(open(f"{P}/batches/batch_004.eval.json"))
des = {d["design_id"]: d for d in json.load(open(f"{P}/designs.json"))["designs"]}
meas = {m["design_id"]: m for m in snap["measurements"]}
BR = snap["frame"]["offset_estimate"]["offset"]

fresh = [p for p in ev["per_design"] if meas[p["design_id"]]["fresh"]]
at102 = collections.Counter(m for p in fresh for m in des[p["design_id"]]["mutations"] if m[1:-1] == "102")
print("fresh designs: %d" % len(fresh))
print("substitutions at position 102 across them: %s" % dict(at102))
print("-> the round is monomorphic at 102; no residue contrast exists inside it")

print("\nhow often had the model seen G102L before it selected this batch?")
for r in (1, 2, 3):
    s = json.load(open(f"{P}/evidence/snapshot_{r:03d}.json"))
    n = [m for m in s["measurements"] if "G102L" in des[m["design_id"]]["mutations"] and m["status"] == "ok"]
    print("  round %d: %d measured designs containing G102L" % (r, len(n)))

by = collections.defaultdict(list)
for p in fresh:
    muts = [m for m in des[p["design_id"]]["mutations"] if m != "G102L"]
    if len(des[p["design_id"]]["mutations"]) == 2 and len(muts) == 1:
        by[muts[0]].append(p["residual"] - BR)
vals = np.array([np.mean(v) for v in by.values()])
print("\nbridge-corrected residual of the G102L doubles, by PARTNER mutation")
print("  %d distinct partners over %d designs -- every class has n=1" % (len(by), sum(len(v) for v in by.values())))
print("  mean %+.3f pKD, sd %.3f, min %+.3f, max %+.3f" % (vals.mean(), vals.std(ddof=1), vals.min(), vals.max()))
print("  partners at or above prediction: %d of %d" % (int((vals >= 0).sum()), vals.size))
print("  partners spread over positions: %s" % dict(collections.Counter(k[1:-1] for k in by)))
print("-> the shortfall is not one partner or one position; it is every partner")

ad_hoc.code:
# The winning recipe, ridge_onehot, is Bayesian linear regression on the raw
# 8x20 one-hot block (core/surrogate.py fit_ridge_onehot, core/encode.py), so it
# carries main effects only and cannot represent an interaction. It saw G102L in
# exactly one measured design. Does the G102L gain it inferred there transfer
# onto new partners the way an additive model must assume?
import json
import numpy as np

P = "projects/demo-trastuzumab"
snap = json.load(open(f"{P}/evidence/snapshot_004.json"))
ev = json.load(open(f"{P}/batches/batch_004.eval.json"))
des = {d["design_id"]: d for d in json.load(open(f"{P}/designs.json"))["designs"]}
meas = {m["design_id"]: m for m in snap["measurements"]}
BR = snap["frame"]["offset_estimate"]["offset"]

s1 = {m["design_id"]: m["value"] for m in json.load(open(f"{P}/evidence/snapshot_001.json"))["measurements"] if m["status"] == "ok"}
singles = {des[d]["mutations"][0]: v for d, v in s1.items() if len(des[d]["mutations"]) == 1}
par = [v for d, v in s1.items() if len(des[d]["mutations"]) == 0][0]

inc = [p for p in ev["per_design"] if p["design_id"] == "497ac31f6a69"][0]
inc_v12 = inc["observed"] - BR
eff_g102l = inc_v12 - singles["A105K"]
print("frames: round-1 scan v1.2 raw; round 4 moved by the bridge %+.4f into the same frame" % BR)
print("parent %.3f pKD.  the one prior G102L design is the incumbent G102L+A105K:" % par)
print("  v1.3 %.3f -> v1.2 frame %.3f.  A105K alone measured %.3f in the scan." % (inc["observed"], inc_v12, singles["A105K"]))
print("  additive effect of G102L implied by it: %+.3f pKD (so the incumbent is additive by construction)" % eff_g102l)

rows = []
for p in ev["per_design"]:
    d = p["design_id"]
    muts = des[d]["mutations"]
    if not meas[d]["fresh"] or "G102L" not in muts or len(muts) != 2:
        continue
    X = [m for m in muts if m != "G102L"][0]
    if X in singles:
        rows.append((X, p["observed"] - BR, par + eff_g102l + (singles[X] - par), singles[X] - par))
obs = np.array([r[1] for r in rows]); add = np.array([r[2] for r in rows]); ep = obs - add
print("\npartners whose own single-mutant effect the round-1 scan measured: %d of 40" % len(rows))
print("  partner   solo effect   measured   additive   shortfall")
for X, o, a, e in sorted(rows, key=lambda r: r[3], reverse=True):
    print("  %-8s  %+9.3f  %9.3f  %9.3f  %+9.3f" % (X, e, o, a, o - a))
print("  mean shortfall %+.3f pKD, sd %.3f; %d of %d reach the additive prediction"
      % (ep.mean(), ep.std(ddof=1), int((ep >= 0).sum()), ep.size))

r3 = [m["value"] for m in json.load(open(f"{P}/evidence/snapshot_003.json"))["measurements"]
      if m["status"] == "ok" and "G102L" in des[m["design_id"]]["mutations"]]
r4 = [p["observed"] - BR for p in ev["per_design"]
      if meas[p["design_id"]]["fresh"] and "G102L" in des[p["design_id"]]["mutations"]]
print("\nG102L designs, both in the v1.2 frame")
print("  round 3: n=%2d  mean %.3f  max %.3f" % (len(r3), np.mean(r3), np.max(r3)))
print("  round 4: n=%2d  mean %.3f  max %.3f" % (len(r4), np.mean(r4), np.max(r4)))
print("  parent is %.3f, so the round-4 G102L doubles average %+.3f over parent"
      % (par, np.mean(r4) - par))
ad_hoc.question: The winning recipe is Bayesian linear regression on the raw 8x20 one-hot block, so it carries main effects only and cannot represent an interaction. It had seen G102L in exactly one measured design. Does the G102L gain it inferred from that one design transfer onto new partners the way an additive model must assume?

hypotheses.claim: The assay moved. Round 4 is the first round run on assay v1.3, a version this project has never characterized, and the shared designs carry a run offset.
hypotheses.reasoning: The bridge is real and its members agree: 3 shared designs, per-design deltas -1.052, -0.899 and -1.092, spread sd 0.102 against a concordance tolerance of 0.342 (2.0 x the round's own read-noise scale 0.171). The estimate is -1.014 pKD, se 0.059. The assay version is v1.3 and known_version_offset is null, so this is a genuine first characterization rather than a drift within a known version -- the situation rule 2 exists for. Partially and not fully supported because of the size: the fresh designs came back -2.046 pKD from prediction and the bridge accounts for half of that. This hypothesis licenses a correction of -1.014 and explicitly does not account for the rest, which h7 and h8 quantify.

hypotheses.claim: One plate ran low and carried the round with it.
hypotheses.reasoning: R4P1 sits at -1.872 over 23 designs and R4P2 at -2.011 over 23. The gap is 0.139 pKD against a standard error of 0.224, z = 0.62. Both plates are low by about the same amount. A plate artifact moves one plate and leaves the other; this moved both equally, which is the signature of something that applies to the whole run.

hypotheses.claim: The assay was unstable while the plates were read, so the round is simply noisy.
hypotheses.reasoning: 45 of 46 scored designs carry two usable reads. The round's own read-noise scale is 0.171 pKD -- in line with round 2's 0.158 -- and not one design's replicates disagree by more than the 0.514 tolerance. The reads are repeatable. Whatever moved this round was in the wells before they were read, so it is an offset or a property of the molecules, not read noise. This also matters for h1: a tight read-noise scale is what makes the bridge's 0.102 spread a genuine agreement rather than three numbers too imprecise to disagree.

hypotheses.claim: A structure-activity effect at one edited position accounts for the round.
hypotheses.reasoning: This test rules out every position except the one that matters, and for that one it has no contrast to offer. Position 102 appears in 43 of 46 scored designs at a mean residual of -1.995, against an overall -1.941: the class is the round, and its 'vs_other_classes' of -0.816 is a comparison against the 3 designs left over. The positions that deviate further are too small to move 42 designs -- 100 at -2.416 over n=4, 104 at -1.571 over n=6, 101 at -0.998 over n=2 with n_fresh=0. The remaining large classes (106 at -1.977 over n=13, 103 at -1.883 over n=10) sit on the overall mean. Reading this as 'not supported' would overclaim, because a cause that is present in 43 of 46 designs is invisible to a test that contrasts classes against each other. Resolving it needed a residue-level cut the library does not have; see the ad hoc list.

hypotheses.claim: The round is a mutation-count effect, as round 2 turned out to be: the model is being asked about a class of design it was not fit on.
hypotheses.reasoning: The test that carried the argument in round 2 is degenerate here. 45 of 46 scored designs are doubles at -1.966 and the only other class is the parent, n=1, at -0.846. A class of one cannot support a contrast. Mutation count is not what distinguishes this batch from its training data -- the model was fit on 130 observations that were mostly doubles -- so this cut has nothing left to find. It is recorded because it is the natural follow-on from decision_002 and a reader will look for it.

hypotheses.claim: In the frame as recorded the model's predictive intervals are unusable over this batch, independently of any offset.
hypotheses.reasoning: Coverage of the 80% interval is 0.065 over 46 designs against 0.823 held out at fit time, and three of the four predicted-value bins are at or near zero. Mean residual -1.941. This is the arithmetic the flag saw and it is not in dispute; it is recorded as the baseline that h7 is measured against, not as evidence for any particular cause. A round can look exactly like this because the ruler changed, and that is what h1 tests.

hypotheses.claim: If the round were nothing but the assay shift the bridge measured, correcting by that estimate would restore coverage.
hypotheses.reasoning: It restores most of it and not all of it. Applying the recorded -1.014 takes coverage from 0.065 to 0.565 and the mean residual from -1.941 to -0.927. That is a large and real recovery -- the opposite of round 2, where the same counterfactual made coverage worse and that is what killed the offset reading there. But nominal is 0.80 and the corrected round does not reach it. The honest statement is the one this test makes: the assay shift is a genuine component of the round and it is not the whole round. The -0.927 that survives the correction is the number this recommendation refuses to explain away.

hypotheses.claim: The same counterfactual, restricted to the fresh designs the anomaly flag was actually computed over.
hypotheses.reasoning: On the 42 fresh designs alone, correcting by the bridge takes coverage from 0.048 to 0.524 and the mean residual from -2.046 to -1.032. So of the -2.046 pKD that tripped a 0.50 trigger, the bridge accounts for -1.014 and -1.032 remains -- almost exactly half each. The leftover is still twice the trigger on its own. Recorded separately from h7 because the flag is defined on this population and a scientist should see the leftover on the same designs the flag was computed from, not diluted by the four carried-over ones.

recommendation.alternative_considered:
no_action or refit_only, correcting nothing. This is the conservative reading and it is what decision_002 concluded, so the precedent in this project runs against correcting. It is rejected on the evidence rather than on the precedent: in round 2 the bridge pointed the wrong way (-0.167 against a +0.765 surprise) and the counterfactual made coverage worse, 0.333 to 0.267; here the bridge points the right way, is six times larger, and the counterfactual takes coverage from 0.065 to 0.565. Round 2's assay version was already characterized; round 4's is new. Declining to correct would also leave round 4 unpoolable with rounds 1-3 under rule 2, which blocks the refit rather than deferring it.

Treating the whole -2.046 as assay -- the reading that would 'fix' the round. Rejected: it needs an offset twice the bridge, and nothing supports one. Rule 4 of the four rules and rule 3 of the procedure both say the shift is the recorded bridge estimate and never a number chosen to make the residuals vanish. The incumbent refutes it directly: at 11.8 pKD, where a scale-dependent shift would be largest, it moved -1.082 and not -2.0.

drop_wells. Rejected: there is no affected group to drop. Both plates agree and no replicate is out of tolerance, so dropping wells would discard the finding rather than an artifact.

A localized structure-activity cliff at one position or residue (h4). Rejected as a description of the remainder, though the mechanism underneath it is real: the shortfall is flat across 40 distinct partner mutations spread over six positions, with every partner class n=1 and no class separating. A cliff is a property of particular residues; this is the same shortfall everywhere, which is what a mis-specified main effect looks like rather than a cliff.

Closing the question decision_002's ruling left open -- whether round 2's on-target singles were on target because they were singles or because they were in the training set. Round 3 answered it and no test here was needed: its 43 fresh designs were all doubles, selected and predicted by a model that had seen 42 doubles, and they came back at coverage 0.745 and mean +0.171. A model that has seen the class predicts the class, including designs it was not trained on. The round-2 reading was extrapolation, not in-sample fit.
recommendation.if_wrong:
The claim is two-part and the parts fail differently.

The offset is wrong if the -1.014 is not a property of the assay run. It is falsified if round 5, run on v1.3 with a v1.3-to-v1.3 bridge, shows a further shift of similar size -- that would make this a drift rather than a version step, and a one-off correction the wrong instrument. It is falsified if re-running any round-4 plate on v1.2 returns the uncorrected values. It is falsified if the three bridge designs turn out to share a plate position or a preparation batch with each other, since all three sit on R4P1. The strongest single check available now is the incumbent, and it is already consistent; if a scientist re-measured the incumbent on v1.3 and got 11.8 rather than 10.75, the whole offset reading collapses.

The reading of the remainder is wrong if the -1.032 is not the additive recipe over-crediting G102L. It is falsified if the refit on the corrected pool still over-predicts G102L doubles by about a pKD, because a refit carrying 40 of them should not. It is falsified if gp_pca64 wins the next bake-off and predicts the round-4 designs well from the same data, which would mean the information was in the features and ridge simply could not use it. It is falsified if a handful of G102L doubles re-tested against fresh single-mutant G102L -- never measured in this project, which is the gap underneath all of this -- show G102L alone at +1.8 rather than the +0.26 implied here, in which case the partners and not the background carry the shortfall.

Both parts would be wrong together if the four re-measured designs are not representative of the batch in some way nobody has checked. They are 4 of 46, all carried over from earlier rounds and all in the training set, and the contrast between them and the fresh designs is confounded between 'measured in both assay versions' and 'the model has seen these'. That confound cannot be resolved inside round 4. It is narrowed by the fact that the three bridge members are the designs defining the correction and the incumbent is not, so the incumbent is the only clean test here and it is a single molecule.
recommendation.rationale:
Correct the frame by the recorded bridge estimate, then refit -- and record that the correction explains half the round and that the other half is a real result the project should act on.

The case for correcting is stronger here than a bridge alone usually makes it. Round 4 is the first round on assay v1.3, a version never characterized, which is exactly the situation rule 2 reserves a bridging set for. The bridge is concordant: three shared designs, spread sd 0.102 against a 0.342 tolerance, estimate -1.014 pKD with se 0.059. Correcting by it takes interval coverage from 0.065 to 0.565. And the corroboration is not circular -- a fourth design was measured in both versions and is not a bridge member: the incumbent 497ac31f6a69, the highest-affinity molecule in the project, read 11.837 in v1.2 and 10.754 in v1.3, a delta of -1.082 against the bridge's -1.014. Across all four re-measured designs the delta varies by 0.193 pKD over a 2.769 pKD span of affinity, a slope of -0.058 pKD per pKD. The shift is additive, it is the same size at the top of the range where this batch was predicted to sit as it is at the parent, and the bridge is therefore the right number to apply to the picks. Without the correction round 4 cannot be pooled with rounds 1-3 at all and every later model would be fit across two rulers.

What the correction does not do is make the round good, and the record should be read for that as much as for the offset. After correcting, the 42 fresh designs are still -1.032 pKD below prediction and coverage is 0.524 against a nominal 0.80. That residue is not the assay: the plates agree with each other (gap 0.139, z 0.62), the reads are repeatable (0 of 45 outside tolerance), and the one high-affinity molecule measured in both versions reproduces the bridge rather than the round. It is the model, and the ad hoc cuts say how. Forty of the 42 fresh designs carry the same mutation, G102L, which the model had seen in exactly one measured design ever -- the round-3 incumbent G102L+A105K at 11.837. The winning recipe is ridge on a one-hot block, additive by construction with no interaction term, so it credited that pair's whole +2.6 pKD to the G102L and A105K main effects and then stacked the G102L term onto 40 new partners. All 40 came back short, mean -1.067, and 38 of 40 below prediction; for the six partners whose solo effect the round-1 scan measured, not one reaches its additive prediction, mean shortfall -1.685 pKD. In the corrected frame the 40 G102L doubles average 9.490 pKD against a parent of 9.230 -- G102L on its own buys about +0.26, not +1.80. The incumbent's affinity is a property of the pair, not of G102L.

That is a finding, not a failure, and correcting it away is exactly what rule 3 of the diagnosis procedure forbids. It is also the decision-relevant fact for the campaign: in the corrected frame the best fresh design of round 4 is 11.245 pKD against an incumbent of 11.837, so round 4 advanced nothing, and the reason is that the optimizer spent 40 of 42 wells re-testing one main effect it had one observation of. The refit will absorb this -- it now has 40 G102L doubles instead of one -- but an additive recipe cannot represent the interaction that makes the incumbent good, so the model will learn to discount G102L rather than to find the next pair. Worth the scientist's attention when ruling: exploration was 2 slots of 48, and the pool around the incumbent is worth sampling as pairs.

Every number above is synthetic -- the landscape is generated, the LIMS is a mock, and the assay is an oracle replaying values with noise.

ad_hoc.code:
# The ruling's question, made quantitative. All three bridge members and the
# incumbent sit on R4P1, so if the -1.014 were a property of that plate rather
# than of the run, the fresh designs on R4P2 -- which carry no cross-version
# anchor at all -- would sit about 1.01 pKD ABOVE the fresh designs on R4P1.
# residual_by_plate --scope fresh gives the gap; this asks what that gap rules
# out, and how large an R4P1-local component it still permits.
import json

import numpy as np

P = "projects/demo-trastuzumab"
snap = json.load(open(f"{P}/evidence/snapshot_004.json"))
ev = json.load(open(f"{P}/batches/batch_004.eval.json"))
meas = {m["design_id"]: m for m in snap["measurements"]}
BR = snap["frame"]["offset_estimate"]["offset"]

print("designs measured on v1.2 and again in this round, by plate:")
for m in snap["measurements"]:
    if not m["fresh"] and m["status"] == "ok":
        print("  %s  %s  bridge=%-5s slot=%s" % (m["design_id"], m["plates"][0], m["bridge"], m["slot"]))
print("-> all four sit on R4P1. R4P2 carries no cross-version anchor, so the")
print("   offset cannot be measured on R4P2 directly -- only inferred from the")
print("   fresh designs, which is what the requested test does.")

g = {}
for p in ev["per_design"]:
    m = meas[p["design_id"]]
    if m["fresh"]:
        g.setdefault(m["plates"][0], []).append(p["residual"])
a, b = np.array(g["R4P1"]), np.array(g["R4P2"])
gap = a.mean() - b.mean()
se = float(np.sqrt(a.var(ddof=1) / a.size + b.var(ddof=1) / b.size))
print("\nfresh designs only (reproduces residual_by_plate --scope fresh):")
print("  R4P1 n=%2d mean %+.3f   R4P2 n=%2d mean %+.3f" % (a.size, a.mean(), b.size, b.mean()))
print("  observed gap P1-P2 %+.3f, se %.3f" % (gap, se))
print("\nthe two readings, as predictions about that gap:")
print("  'the shift is the run'                    -> gap  0.000 : observed is %.1f se away" % (abs(gap - 0.0) / se))
print("  'the shift is the plate the bridge is on' -> gap %+.3f : observed is %.1f se away"
      % (BR, abs(gap - BR) / se))
print("\nan R4P1-local component A of the bridge estimate is bounded by the gap:")
print("  A = %+.3f +/- %.3f (1 se); |A| < %.3f at 2 se, against a bridge estimate of %+.3f"
      % (gap, se, abs(gap) + 2 * se, BR))
print("  so at most %.0f%% of the correction could be plate rather than run, and the"
      % (100 * (abs(gap) + 2 * se) / abs(BR)))
print("  point estimate says %.0f%%." % (100 * abs(gap) / abs(BR)))
print("\nnote: the snapshot records plate, not well. A within-plate position")
print("effect is not testable from the project directory.")

# Equal residuals on two plates only mean equal displacement if the two plates
# hold the same kind of design. core/acquisition.py assign_plates lays a batch
# out in slot order, 24 per plate, so R4P1 took the controls, the replicates,
# the two exploration slots and the first 18 picks while R4P2 took the last 24
# picks. If picks are ordered by acquisition score the plates differ in what
# the model expected of them. Are they comparable, and does the null gap
# survive restricting to like for like?
import collections
import json

import numpy as np

P = "projects/demo-trastuzumab"
snap = json.load(open(f"{P}/evidence/snapshot_004.json"))
batch = json.load(open(f"{P}/batches/batch_004.json"))
ev = json.load(open(f"{P}/batches/batch_004.eval.json"))
des = {d["design_id"]: d for d in json.load(open(f"{P}/designs.json"))["designs"]}
meas = {m["design_id"]: m for m in snap["measurements"]}
slots = {s["design_id"]: s for s in batch["slots"]}

rows = [(meas[p["design_id"]]["plates"][0], p) for p in ev["per_design"] if meas[p["design_id"]]["fresh"]]

print("fresh designs, what each plate is made of")
for pl in ("R4P1", "R4P2"):
    rs = [r for r in rows if r[0] == pl]
    pred = np.array([p["pred_mean"] for _, p in rs])
    print("  %-6s n=%2d  G102L %2d  pred %.2f-%.2f (mean %.2f)  pred_sd %.3f  extrap %d  %s"
          % (pl, len(rs), sum("G102L" in des[p["design_id"]]["mutations"] for _, p in rs),
             pred.min(), pred.max(), pred.mean(),
             np.mean([p["pred_sd"] for _, p in rs]),
             sum(p["extrapolation"] for _, p in rs),
             dict(collections.Counter(slots[p["design_id"]]["slot"] for _, p in rs))))

print("\npartner positions (the non-G102L mutation), by plate")
for pl in ("R4P1", "R4P2"):
    c = collections.Counter(m[1:-1] for q, p in rows if q == pl
                            for m in des[p["design_id"]]["mutations"] if m != "G102L")
    print("  %-6s %s" % (pl, dict(sorted(c.items()))))


def gap(rs, label):
    a = np.array([p["residual"] for pl, p in rs if pl == "R4P1"])
    b = np.array([p["residual"] for pl, p in rs if pl == "R4P2"])
    se = float(np.sqrt(a.var(ddof=1) / a.size + b.var(ddof=1) / b.size))
    d = a.mean() - b.mean()
    print("  %-38s P1 n=%2d %+.3f | P2 n=%2d %+.3f | gap %+.3f se %.3f (%.1f se from zero)"
          % (label, a.size, a.mean(), b.size, b.mean(), d, se, abs(d) / se))


print("\nthe gap under restrictions that remove the ways the plates differ")
gap(rows, "all fresh")
gap([r for r in rows if slots[r[1]["design_id"]]["slot"] == "pick"], "pick slots only")
gap([r for r in rows if "G102L" in des[r[1]["design_id"]]["mutations"]], "G102L doubles only")
lo = max(min(p["pred_mean"] for pl, p in rows if pl == "R4P1"),
         min(p["pred_mean"] for pl, p in rows if pl == "R4P2"))
hi = min(max(p["pred_mean"] for pl, p in rows if pl == "R4P1"),
         max(p["pred_mean"] for pl, p in rows if pl == "R4P2"))
gap([r for r in rows if lo <= r[1]["pred_mean"] <= hi], "overlapping predicted range %.2f-%.2f" % (lo, hi))
ad_hoc.question: Equal residuals on two plates only mean equal displacement if the plates hold the same kind of design, and assign_plates lays a batch out in slot order rather than at random. Are the two halves comparable, and does the null gap survive restricting to like for like?

hypotheses.claim: The -1.014 pKD bridge estimate is a property of R4P1 -- the plate all three bridge members sit on -- and not of the run, so applying it to all 46 measurements would move R4P2 by a number nothing on R4P2 measured.
hypotheses.reasoning: This is the test the ruling asked for, and it answers the question it was asked to answer. With the four carried-over designs removed -- the three bridge members and the incumbent, all four of which sit on R4P1 -- the plates are 19 fresh designs on R4P1 at -2.089 and 23 on R4P2 at -2.011. The gap is 0.079 pKD against a standard error of 0.218, z = 0.36. R4P2 carries no cross-version design at all, so under the reading being tested its fresh designs should be displaced only by whatever is not the plate-1 offset, which means sitting about 1.01 pKD above R4P1's. They sit 0.08 below. The observed gap is 0.4 se from the run reading and 4.3 se from the plate reading (ad hoc 1). Removing the bridge members moved the gap from 0.139 to 0.079, so they were not what was holding the two plate means together. What this does not establish is that no plate component exists: the gap resolves 0.218 pKD per se, so a component up to 0.51 pKD -- half the correction -- survives at 2 se, and the snapshot records plate but not well, so within-plate position is untestable here.

hypotheses.claim: The same test over every scored design, so the fresh-only cut can be read against the population pass 1 reported.
hypotheses.reasoning: Unchanged from pass 1 and repeated here so the two scopes sit side by side: 46 designs, R4P1 at -1.872 over 23 and R4P2 at -2.011 over 23, gap 0.139 against se 0.224. The carried-over designs pull R4P1's mean up because the model predicts them well, which is why the fresh-only cut the ruling asked for is the right population for this question: it takes the four designs that are both the evidence for the offset and the best-fit designs in the round out of the plate comparison entirely.

hypotheses.claim: The assay moved. Round 4 is the first round on assay v1.3, a version this project has never characterized, and the shared designs carry a run offset.
hypotheses.reasoning: Re-run unchanged, because the correction this pass recommends rests on it. Three shared designs, per-design deltas -1.052, -0.899 and -1.092, spread sd 0.102 against a concordance tolerance of 0.342, estimate -1.014 pKD with se 0.059. Assay version v1.3 with known_version_offset null, so this is a first characterization rather than drift within a known version. Partially supported for the same reason as in pass 1 -- the fresh designs came back -2.046 and the bridge accounts for half of it -- and now with the plate question answered as well: h9 says the displacement the bridge measured on R4P1 is present in equal size on a plate that contains no bridge member, which is what makes it a run property rather than a property of three wells.

hypotheses.claim: In the frame as recorded, the model's intervals are unusable over the fresh designs -- the baseline the correction is measured against.
hypotheses.reasoning: Coverage 0.048 over the 42 fresh designs against a nominal 0.80, mean residual -2.046. This is the arithmetic the flag saw, restricted to the population the flag is defined on. It is the baseline for h13 and not evidence for any cause.

hypotheses.claim: If the round were nothing but the assay shift the bridge measured, correcting by that estimate would restore coverage over the fresh designs.
hypotheses.reasoning: Correcting by the recorded -1.014 takes the fresh designs from coverage 0.048 to 0.524 and the mean residual from -2.046 to -1.032. Half the round is the assay and half is not, and the -1.032 that survives is the number this recommendation still refuses to explain away. Nothing in this pass changed it: the plate test moved the case for the correction, not the size of the leftover.

recommendation.alternative_considered:
Not correcting, which is the branch the ruling named: 'if it is not, say so and do not correct.' The condition did not obtain. Had R4P2's fresh designs come back about a pKD above R4P1's, the bridge would have been measuring three wells on one plate and the correct output would have been no_action with confidence 'refuses'. They came back 0.079 below, 0.4 se from equality. Declining to correct anyway would leave round 4 unpoolable with rounds 1-3 under rule 2 and block the refit rather than defer it.

Correcting per plate rather than uniformly -- R4P1 by the bridge and R4P2 by the bridge minus the measured gap. Rejected on two grounds. The gap is 0.4 se from zero, so a per-plate correction would be fitting read noise, and the skill's rule is that the shift applied is the recorded bridge estimate and never a number assembled while reading the round. import_round takes one offset, which is the same rule enforced in code.

drop_wells, on the reading that R4P1 is compromised because the bridge sits there. Rejected: the two plates agree, so there is no affected group, and dropping R4P1 would discard the only four cross-version designs in the round along with the evidence for any correction at all.

Treating the whole -2.046 as assay. Rejected in pass 1 and unchanged: it needs an offset twice the bridge, and the incumbent at 11.8 pKD -- where a scale-dependent shift would be largest -- moved -1.082 and not -2.0.

A localized structure-activity cliff as the description of the remainder. Rejected in pass 1: the shortfall is flat across 40 distinct partners over six positions, which is a mis-specified main effect rather than a cliff.
recommendation.if_wrong:
The plate reading is wrong if the two plates are displaced equally for two different reasons that happen to cancel. It is falsified if a restriction exists under which the plates separate: pick slots only, G102L doubles only and the overlapping predicted range were tried and none moved the gap past 0.8 se, but a cut nobody has thought of could. It is falsified if the round-4 plates differ in something the project directory does not record -- reagent lot, read order, operator -- in which case the equality is a coincidence of two offsets. The clean version of this check does not exist inside round 4 and cannot be built from it: it needs a bridge member on R4P2, which is what the layout change above would buy.

The correction is wrong in size if a plate-1-local component is real. The gap bounds it at 0.51 pKD at 2 se, and at the top of that range the uniform correction over-corrects R4P2 by half a pKD and the assay/model split of the round moves with it -- the leftover attributed to the model would be smaller on R4P2 and unchanged on R4P1. It is falsified by round 5: run on v1.3 with bridge members on both plates, a plate-1 component shows up as a plate-dependent bridge estimate. A further shift of similar size in round 5 would instead make this drift rather than a version step, and a one-off correction the wrong instrument. Re-running any round-4 plate on v1.2 and getting the uncorrected values back falsifies the whole offset reading; re-measuring the incumbent on v1.3 and getting 11.8 rather than 10.75 does the same.

Nothing in this pass tests within-plate position, because the snapshot carries plate and not well. If the three bridge wells are adjacent on R4P1 and the plate has an edge or a gradient, this pass cannot see it and neither can any of the five diagnostics. The results export carries a well column; that cut is available to someone with the export and was not available here.

The reading of the remainder is wrong if the -1.032 is not the additive recipe over-crediting G102L. It is falsified if the refit on the corrected pool still over-predicts G102L doubles by about a pKD with 40 of them in hand; if gp_pca64 wins the next bake-off and predicts the round-4 designs well from the same data; or if a fresh single-mutant G102L -- never measured in this project -- comes back at +1.8 over parent rather than the +0.26 implied here, in which case the partners and not the background carry the shortfall.
recommendation.rationale:
The test came back the way the correction needs, so the recommendation is unchanged: correct the frame by the recorded bridge estimate of -1.014 pKD under this record's authority, re-run evaluate_prior, then refit -- and keep the finding that the correction explains half the round and the model explains the other half.

What was asked for. residual_by_plate --scope fresh takes out all four carried-over designs, which matters more than the ruling assumed: not only the three bridge members but the incumbent too sit on R4P1, so R4P2 has no cross-version anchor of any kind and is the clean test. Its 23 fresh designs sit at -2.011 against R4P1's 19 at -2.089. The gap is 0.079 pKD, se 0.218, z = 0.36. If the -1.014 were carried by the plate the bridge happens to be on, R4P2's fresh designs would sit about 1.01 pKD above R4P1's; that prediction is 4.3 se from what was measured, while the run reading is 0.4 se from it (ad hoc 1). Both halves of the round are displaced by the same amount, and one of those halves never saw a bridge well.

The ways the two plates are not interchangeable were checked rather than assumed, because assign_plates fills in slot order: R4P1 took the controls, the replicates, both exploration slots and 17 scored picks, R4P2 took 23 picks. Restricting to pick slots only, the gap is 0.166 (0.8 se); to G102L doubles only, the same 0.166; to the overlapping predicted range 10.29-10.90, 0.095 (0.5 se). No restriction moves it anywhere near 1.01 (ad hoc 2).

What the test does not settle, stated rather than glossed. It bounds a plate-1-local component of the bridge estimate at 0.079 +/- 0.218, so at 2 se a component up to 0.51 pKD -- half the correction -- is not excluded, and if one exists the uniform correction over-corrects R4P2 by that much while leaving R4P1 right. The point estimate is 0.08 pKD, below the round's read noise of 0.171. Nothing here addresses within-plate position: the snapshot records plate and not well, so that question cannot be answered from the project directory at all.

One thing this pass turned up that outlives round 4. The bridge sitting entirely on one plate is not bad luck, it is structural: core/acquisition.py assign_plates lays the batch out in slot order at 24 per plate, and the controls and replicates are the first slots, so every round of this template puts its entire bridging set on plate 1 and every future offset estimate has exactly the blind spot this ruling pointed at. Round 4 can answer it only because both plates happen to hold the same kind of design. Splitting the bridge across plates from round 5 would make the offset estimate plate-robust by construction. That is a template change and not a run choice, so it is flagged here for a ruling rather than made.

The rest of the diagnosis stands as written in pass 1 and is what the campaign should act on. After correcting, the 42 fresh designs are still -1.032 pKD below prediction at coverage 0.524. That residue is the additive recipe over-crediting G102L, which it had seen in exactly one measured design -- the round-3 incumbent -- and then stacked onto 40 new partners, all of which came back short. In the corrected frame the best fresh design of round 4 is 11.245 pKD against an incumbent of 11.837, so round 4 advanced nothing, and the reason is that 40 of 42 wells re-tested one main effect the model had one observation of.

Every number here is synthetic -- the landscape is generated, the LIMS is a mock, and the assay is an oracle replaying values with noise.

trigger: 42 fresh designs came back a mean -2.046 pKD below the model's prediction, se 0.108, z -18.96, against a trigger of 0.50. Round 4 is the first round this project has run on assay v1.3 and known_version_offset is null, so the round carries both a possible uncharacterized assay shift and 42 new designs, and the flag cannot tell them apart. The sign is negative: the round came back worse than forecast.
